metadata.datasource: Measured off Kodak H-1-5222 (3-22), EASTMAN DOUBLE-X Negative Film 5222 / 7222: its characteristic curve for D-96 at 21 C, 6.5 min (gamma 0.66), the development its exposure index names ('for development to a gamma of 0.65'), daylight exposure, Status M (blue) density; its spectral sensitivity and MTF off the vector plots of the edition of 10/2003 (H-1-5222), which the 3-22 edition's bitmaps repeat. Characteristic curve laid on agx's axis with mid-grey at log H -1.398 on the sheet's absolute axis, Kodak's normal exposure, 10/EI at EI 250 daylight: the sheet's tungsten exposure table (f/5.6 at 200 footcandles, 24 fps, 170-degree shutter) gives an 18% grey card 0.049-0.050 lux-seconds at EI 200 through a lens of ISO 2720's q = 0.65, which is 10/EI. The curve's own ISO speed point is ISO 301; base + fog 0.223. Continued at its final gradient for 0.8 decades past the last plotted exposure. Spectral sensitivity: the D = 1.0 over gross fog curve (equal-energy, erg/cm^2, effective exposure 1.4 s, D-96 to the recommended control gamma, diffuse visual), drawn from 420 to 660 nm and continued to 400 and 670 nm by the D = 0.3 curve's own shape, joined where it stops. The base is grey (its antihalation), 0.20 by the sheet. One silver layer, carried as three identical channels.
